title: Alphabet stock has its biggest one day drop after earnings
summary: Alphabet shares fell about 12.6% on Thursday after its third quarter report. Reports say profit per share came in at $2.12, below the $3.02 analysts expected, while spending on AI equipment was larger than the cash the business produced. Its cloud unit grew very fast.
why: When a company spends more than it earns in cash, investors worry about how long that can last. Even a great cloud business did not calm that worry, and a big drop like this shows how much a stock can move on one report.

title: Amazon's cloud speeds up to 39% growth, but spending worries linger
summary: Amazon reported after the close that its AWS cloud unit grew 39% from a year ago, its fastest pace in nearly five years. Profit per share of $1.89 was a little under what analysts expected. Reports disagree on how far the stock fell in after hours trading.
why: AWS rents out computer power, which AI needs a lot of, so faster growth is a good sign. But Amazon is also spending huge sums on new data centers, and investors are watching whether that spending pays off.

title: Eli Lilly raises its yearly sales forecast after a strong quarter
summary: Eli Lilly said third quarter sales rose 39% to $24.4 billion, led by its diabetes and weight loss medicines Mounjaro and Zepbound. It raised its full year sales forecast to $91 billion to $92 billion. The stock rose about 6.6% on Thursday.
why: A company raising its own forecast tells investors it expects to keep selling more. Still, Lilly said it sold more units at lower prices, so it is worth watching whether price cuts slow future profit.

title: The Fed keeps interest rates unchanged in a split vote
summary: The Federal Reserve left its main rate at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday. Two officials voted to raise it by a quarter point, and reports say markets now see a good chance of a hike in December. The 10 year Treasury yield was reported near 5%.
why: Higher interest rates make borrowing cost more and can make safer investments like bonds look more attractive compared with stocks. That is why rate news can move the whole market, especially fast growing tech companies.
